entries.summary: Implement adaptive duplex behavior: when downlink audio is playing, reduce or pause uplink capture/encoding to avoid LTE contention; resume capture after playback. Add LED state to indicate “receiving” vs “recording.”
entries.note: Adaptive duplex uplink in firmware/nrf9160 (src/main.c + audio_opus.c/h). While downlink audio is playing (dl_jitter_fill>0 plus a 300 ms hangover): DUCK halves the uplink Opus target via new pendant_opus_stream_set_bitrate() (16000 -> 8000 bps), and HOLD stops feeding the encoder once the 7 KiB uplink FIFO passes 60% fill (releases below 40%, or immediately when playback ends), reserving ~2.8 KiB for the user's next question. Chose duck-not-mute because barge-in is server-side: a fully paused uplink would make the agent uninterruptible. New counters duck_ms and uplink_held added to the 'Conversation stats:' printk. RAM before 202676 B (95.78%) / FLASH 382952 B (64.93%); RAM after 202700 B (95.79%) / FLASH 383312 B (64.99%) — +24 B RAM, +360 B flash, 8908 B headroom left. FLASHED to the DK and verified running: 61 s duplex conversation, max_loop_ms=22, tx_starved=0, mic_drops=0, uplink_drops=0, fifo_left=293, new fields print (duck_ms=0 uplink_held=0). NOT YET EXERCISED: that run had decoded_packets=0 (agent never spoke, silent room), so the duck/hold path itself is unverified on hardware — it only proves the adaptation does not engage spuriously. Needs a conversation with real speech to confirm.

entries.note: cloud-relay/serverBrowser.js + serverBrowser.test.js (35 tests, all pass). Cloudflare Browser Run Quick Actions: readPublicPage() prefers the Workers env.BROWSER binding (no token in-Worker, needs compat_date >= 2026-03-24; ours is 2026-07-31) and falls back to REST (CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID/CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN) for the node relay. wrangler.jsonc now declares the browser binding; dry-run confirms 'env.BROWSER -> Browser Run' and the module bundles for workerd. VERIFIED LIVE against account 137c3d31 with the existing wrangler OAuth token (scope 'browser (write)'): example.com read in 2.25s browser-time, docs page sanitized+truncated, private/loopback URLs refused before any egress. PLAN REALITY (measured, not read): this account is Workers FREE, so Browser Run allows 1 Quick Action per 10s (observed 429 + Retry-After: 10 on a back-to-back call) and 10 browser-minutes/day. Workers Paid lifts that to 10/s and unmetered. No upgrade is required to ship; it only bounds throughput. Read-only public web is a CAPABILITY boundary, not a permission gate: the edge browser holds no owner cookies and is on no owner network, so logins and LAN pages route to browser_run_actions (Mac extension) - the result carries a hint saying exactly that, plus a login-wall heuristic. Output sanitization: front-matter title lifted, zero-width/bidi-override chars stripped (hidden-instruction vector), control chars removed, base64 data: URIs collapsed, 12k char cap, results flagged untrusted:true. NOT WIRED: openaiRealtimeVoice.js/server.js/jobs.js were owned by a concurrent agent. The exact 3-file wiring patch (openaiRealtimeVoice.js import + READ_WEB_PAGE_TOOL as the 6th tool + read_web_page dispatch branch; openaiRealtimeVoice.test.js tool-list assertion; fleetContext.js routing line + capability line) is in the report; verified with git apply --check and by running the full 135-test suite against a wired copy - all pass.

entries.summary: Add transactional desktop jobs: each plan has a preview, stable job/action IDs, preconditions (expected app/path/hash), checkpoints, result receipts, and compensating undo where possible. On retry, skip completed action IDs rather than replaying clicks or shell commands. Prefer accessibility selectors and declarative APIs over coordinates.
entries.note: Built the receipt/undo half only. NO gates, NO approval prompts, NO preconditions — nothing added here can refuse or skip an action, per owner policy. New local-agent/actionReceipts.js; executor.js now wraps every dispatch: observeBeforeAction(action) runs first (pure observation, swallows all errors, its verdict is never read), then buildActionReceipt() attaches a receipt to every result — successful or failed. Receipt carries: content-addressed actionId (stable across a re-run of the same plan; positional index would not be, because the orchestrator hands the executor one action at a time), unique receiptId, effect read|write, what was touched (paths, urls, apps, shell commands, email recipients, clipboard, settings with before/after), duration, and an honest reversibility verdict with reversedBy or irreversibleReason. Reversibility now lives in ONE place: undo.js imports describeReversibility() so the receipt the owner reads and the decision undo makes cannot disagree; jobs recorded before receipts existed fall back to the raw result fields, so old history stays undoable. COMPENSATING UNDO: observeBeforeAction snapshots any file a write_file/create_note/delete_path/copy_path/move_path is about to clobber into ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace/.undo (bounded at 8 MB; directories and oversize files are recorded as irreversible WITH the reason rather than silently half-copied). This makes delete_path — previously permanent — undoable, and fixes a real data-loss bug: undo used to answer 'yes, reversible' for a write_file that OVERWROTE an existing file and then reverse it by DELETING that file, destroying content the agent never wrote. Now it restores the exact prior bytes. Surfaced at GET /jobs (receipts per job), new GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts (counts + per-step undo verdict + snapshot vault path), and inside GET /ops/snapshot so the dashboard and relay see them too. describeUndoability now returns steps[] and irreversible[] with reasons, so 'why can't I undo this?' has an answer. Verified live end to end: overwrote a hand-written file via POST /execute, receipt showed reversible=true reversedBy='restore snapshot', POST /jobs/:id/undo restored the original content. Tests: actionReceipts.test.js (16); full suite 499/499.

Enable a bounded audio-retention sweeper and per-job deletion controls: default to short retention for generated briefings, delete expired R2 objects and D1 pointers idempotently, and expose a dashboard ‘delete now’ action. Keep owner-pinned items separate with an explicit expiry.
entries.note: NOT IMPLEMENTED — cloud-relay/ was owned by another agent during this pass. Read-only gap analysis + patch plan follows. WHAT ALREADY EXISTS: cloud-relay/audioRetention.js has the policy, expiry math, per-item deleteStoredAudio (modes audio|record), and sweepExpiredAudio; routes exist at server.js:1850 DELETE /v1/ops/audio-captures/:captureId/audio, :1974 DELETE /v1/ops/history/:pipelineId/audio, :2105 GET /v1/ops/audio-retention, :2137 POST /v1/ops/audio-retention/sweep; 11 tests in audioRetention.test.js. WHAT IS MISSING, in priority order. (1) THE SWEEP CANNOT CLEAR A BACKLOG — most serious. audioRetention.js:173 clamps store.listJobs to 100 (jobQuery.js:8 JOB_LIST_MAX_LIMIT), making AUDIO_RETENTION_SWEEP_MAX_BATCH=200 unreachable; listJobs sorts created_at DESC (d1Store.js:566), so the sweep scans the NEWEST 100 captures — the ones least likely to be expired — and passes no 'before' cursor even though jobQuery.js:20 supports keyset pagination. Past 100 rows, sweeps report 0 expired forever while the backlog below the window is unreachable. GET /v1/ops/audio-retention (server.js:2111) under-reports for the same reason. FIX: thread a cursor into sweepExpiredAudio, return nextCursor, and add an oldest-first query mode (or loop until drained). Add the test that exposes it: >100 rows through sweepExpiredAudio itself — the existing batch-cap test at audioRetention.test.js:106 calls selectExpiredAudioCaptures directly and bypasses the clamp, which is why the bug is invisible. (2) NO AUTOMATION. sweepExpiredAudio's only caller is the manual POST route (server.js:2146). cloudflare-worker/worker.js:6 exports only fetch — no scheduled(); wrangler.jsonc has no triggers/crons and ships AUDIO_RETENTION_SWEEP_ENABLED:false. FIX: add scheduled() + a crons trigger, keep the opt-in flag as the safety. (3) ONE BAD OBJECT ABORTS THE WHOLE SWEEP. The loop at audioRetention.js:195 has no try/catch, the route has none, and server.js has no Express error middleware — an R2 delete that throws discards the report for every capture already processed. FIX: per-item try/catch, collect failures into a failed[] array. (4) IDEMPOTENCY DEFECTS. A second delete of the same capture still runs updateJob (audioRetention.js:141) and CLOBBERS the original audioDeletedAt/audioDeletedReason; and when deleteAudioCaptureObject returns false (untrusted key, audioStorage.js:130, or unbound bucket) deleteStoredAudio nulls audioRef anyway, orphaning the R2 object forever while reporting ok:true. FIX: skip the update when audioStorage is already 'deleted', and do not null audioRef when the object delete returned false — surface it as orphaned. (5) NO OWNER-PIN. Zero implementation anywhere (the 'pinned' hits in browserSessions.js are browser tabs). createAudioCapture (jobs.js:21) has no retention-override field; expiry is derived purely from createdAt + one global maxAgeMs. Storage is schema-free JSON in relay_jobs.data, so FIX is: add pinned/retainUntil to the capture, honour it in isAudioCaptureExpired, and expose a pin toggle. (6) NO SHORT RETENTION FOR GENERATED AUDIO. 'briefing' appears nowhere in the repo; generated TTS is stored as an audio_capture that differs only by role:'reply' (server.js:1070, pendantConverse.js:400), bolted on outside createAudioCapture, and retention has one global 30-day window (config.js:27). FIX: AUDIO_RETENTION_GENERATED_MAX_AGE_MS + a branch on capture.role. (7) PER-RUN DELETE ORPHANS THE REPLY. DELETE /v1/ops/history/:pipelineId/audio (server.js:1974) deletes only detail.capture — the owner's voice — and never the linked replyCaptureId, unlike the GET route which handles ?voice=reply (server.js:1949). FIX: add the voice param to DELETE. (8) NO DASHBOARD 'DELETE NOW'. Both dashboards are playback-only: the ops SPA (src/ops/OpsApp.jsx:946, api.js has no audio delete and points at the Mac agent, not /v1/ops) and SvelteKit (routes/api/history/[pipelineId]/audio/+server.ts exports GET only). entries.summary: Add a durable browser job runner with two backends: the authenticated Safari bridge for owner-private pages and Cloudflare Browser Run for public pages. Represent each step as navigate/read/extract/click/type, persist evidence (URL, title, timestamp, selected text), retry transient failures, and expose a job result stream to the planner.
Check my logged-in web accounts for anything urgent, summarize it, and draft (but do not send) any replies that need my attention.
Every weekday morning, check my logged-in calendar, task board, and travel reservations, then tell me the three things I need to know and prepare a suggested plan.
Watch this logged-in page for a meaningful change and tell me when it happens, with the before-and-after evidence.
Every weekday at 8:30, prepare a concise workday brief: today's calendar, unread mail grouped by urgency, and the top three actions; save it as an audio briefing I can play later.
When I say 'triage my inbox', classify unread mail into urgent, reply soon, reference, and noise, draft replies for the first two categories, and show me a reviewable list without sending anything.
Keep a daily 'closeout' routine: at 5:30 PM, summarize unfinished calendar items and the notes/files I touched today, then create a short checklist for tomorrow.
Watch my chosen logged-in web pages once a day and tell me only what changed; prepare drafts for any follow-up forms, but stop before submitting.
“Check the weather and read the highlights to me.”

Add a Jobs inbox shared by web, menubar, and iOS: each job shows status, source links, last update, evidence snippets, sensitivity, proposed actions, and a prominent 'ready to send/submit' preview. Include per-routine pause/run-now/edit controls and a delivery preference for pendant audio.

Add a unified Jobs inbox shared by web, menubar, and iOS: queued/running/completed/failed jobs, source timestamps, concise result, audio-play button, retry, cancel where safe, and a per-action audit trail. Separate 'draft ready' from 'executed' states.

Make browser work explicitly two-phase: 'inspect' returns a concise result with citations and a proposed action; 'apply' repeats the exact destination, fields/content, and irreversible effect, then waits for owner confirmation. Allow the owner to say 'continue' only for that displayed proposal, while reversible navigation/filling can proceed immediately.

Add typed, read-only observability endpoints for job execution: running apps, foreground app, accessibility state, browser tabs, and allowlisted directory listings, plus structured per-action result/error records for existing execution.

Replace raw browser-page insertion into context with expiring, source-backed facts: store only normalized facts plus source URL, observedAt, confidence, and sensitivity class; keep full extracts in short-lived encrypted job artifacts and prune them automatically.

Replace per-surface hand-written fleetContext prompt sections with a compact, typed context service that returns only task-relevant facts, each with source, timestamp, confidence, and expiry; automatically prune stale session detail and raw audio references.

Add an asynchronous job router: realtime handles only immediate conversational acknowledgement and dispatch; a cheaper background model handles calendar/mail/file summarization, classification, and draft generation; deterministic code performs collection, limits, redaction, and formatting.

Add a Worker-side scheduler using Cron Triggers and Durable Object alarms to run routines even when the Mac is asleep, with a simple queue that delegates to the Mac when it’s online or performs server-side tasks when possible.
Every weekday morning, give me a short audio brief of today's calendar, unread important mail, weather, and any browser jobs that finished overnight.
Check my authenticated browser accounts for anything that needs my attention, then put findings in a review queue instead of changing anything.
When I say 'clean up my desktop', group obvious screenshots and downloads into dated folders, but show me the proposed moves first.
Before my next meeting, prepare a one-page brief from the calendar invite, recent related mail, and approved web sources, save it to my Mac, and tell me where it is.
Every weekday morning, give me a short brief of today's calendar, unread important mail, and the one thing I should prepare for; let me hear it on the pendant and see links on the dashboard.
When I say 'research this' or schedule a topic, investigate the web, summarize the best sources, and leave a cited note and a short audio briefing for later.
Clean up my Downloads: identify duplicate, temporary, and likely finished files, show me a proposed plan, then move only the approved items into an archive folder.
Turn my unread mail into a priority list and draft replies for the top three, but never send anything without showing me the drafts first.
“When I get back to my desk, summarize what happened while I was away and queue anything urgent.”
“Remind me every weekday at 5 to shut down and summarize what I did today.”
“Read me the top three things I should care about right now.”

Ship a unified Jobs inbox across web, menubar, and iOS showing queued/running/completed/failed work, source account, evidence links, data sensitivity, cost estimate, cancellation, and approval requests; add a compact 'pending while Mac asleep' state.

Make every Mac plan two-phase by default: first return a concise preview with affected app/files/URLs and expected side effects, then execute only the safe subset automatically; preserve the owner’s current foreground app and use accessibility-targeted actions rather than stealing focus. Add a single spoken 'undo last plan' for supported reversible operations.

Add a mandatory server-side confirmation broker around POST /execute: classify each action batch, require a short-lived token for external side effects (send, purchase, delete, overwrite, shell, AppleScript), and support dry-run previews plus idempotency keys. Keep reversible local actions fast, but make FULL_CONTROL_MODE unable to bypass this policy.

Add a real policy gate around POST /execute even when FULL_CONTROL_MODE is enabled: classify actions into read-only, reversible, and consequential; require a short-lived confirmation token for sending messages, deleting/overwriting files, purchases, credential changes, and external side effects. Keep an owner-configurable allowlist for harmless routines, and write an append-only audit record with before/after and rollback metadata where possible.

Replace hand-written per-surface fleetContext prompt sections with a single typed context service that stores compact facts, provenance, sensitivity, TTL, and last-used timestamps; retrieve only task-relevant facts and automatically prune stale/duplicate session text.

Replace per-surface hand-written fleetContext prompt sections with a shared, typed context compiler: retrieve only task-relevant entities/relations, attach confidence and freshness, cap tokens per tier, and summarize/archive stale session details. Keep private data scoped by surface and purpose.

Split work into a cheap asynchronous planner/classifier, deterministic Mac/browser executors, and realtime only for live dialogue and ambiguous confirmation. Add budgets, deadlines, cancellation, and partial-result delivery to every job.

Add a first-class scheduler/queue for delayed and recurring work in the relay, backed by Durable Objects (alarms) or Worker Cron. Provide a routine store (D1) and a delivery mechanism that can produce an audio summary stored in R2 and a dashboard notification.
